name: Lengthening over nail (LON)
summary: Hybrid limb-lengthening technique that pairs an external fixator with an intramedullary nail to shorten frame time; studied in cosmetic and non-cosmetic series.
lead: Lengthening over nail (LON) is a limb-lengthening technique in which an intramedullary nail is placed in the bone and an external fixator is used for distraction, after which the fixator is removed while the nail remains . It was developed to minimise the time patients wear a frame during femur lengthening .

name: Femur vs tibia lengthening
summary: The choice of which leg bone to lengthen: femur gets the larger, better-documented gains, tibia is usually staged later and carries its own nerve and ankle risks.
lead: Femur vs tibia lengthening refers, in looksmaxxing and limb-lengthening communities, to the decision about which bone segment to lengthen surgically for height: the femur (thigh bone), the tibia (shin bone), or both, usually in stages. Both operations use distraction osteogenesis, in which a bone is cut and the pieces are slowly pulled apart so that new bone forms in the gap, at a rate commonly given as about 1 mm per day .
claims: The femur gives more height with fewer complications, so it should come first.
Tibial lengthening carries more risk to nerves and the ankle.
Both bones can be lengthened together for a larger total gain.

name: Leg lengthening medical tourism
summary: Travelling abroad for cheaper cosmetic leg lengthening, with lower prices traded against follow-up-care and regulation questions.
lead: Leg lengthening medical tourism is the practice of travelling to another country for cosmetic limb-lengthening surgery, typically to reduce cost. Looksmaxxing and height-focused communities discuss destinations including Turkey, Asia and Poland as alternatives to clinics in the United States and Western Europe .

name: Leuprolide (GnRH agonist puberty blocker)
summary: A prescription GnRH agonist that pauses puberty in medical settings; its use to extend growth in short-stature protocols is investigational and unproven.
lead: Leuprolide (leuprorelin) is a synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonist, administered by injection, that lowers testosterone and estradiol by desensitising pituitary GnRH receptors . It was patented in 1973 and introduced for medical use in 1985 . It is approved for advanced prostate cancer, and elsewhere for endometriosis, fibroids and central precocious puberty .

name: Bone age X-ray (growth plate check)
summary: A hand and wrist X-ray used by pediatric clinicians to gauge skeletal maturity, and by height-focused forum users to ask whether growth plates are still open.
lead: Bone age is the degree of skeletal maturity, usually assessed from a radiograph of the left hand and wrist and expressed as the age at which an average child shows the same development . It differs from chronological age and is used to help diagnose and monitor conditions such as constitutional growth delay, precocious puberty, thyroid disease and growth hormone deficiency, and to predict adult height .
claims: A wrist X-ray shows whether you can still grow taller.
Anabolic steroids, growth hormone and peptides can accelerate bone age and fuse the plates early.
A stack of a senolytic, a bioregulator peptide and a PTH analogue could keep bone age younger.

name: Morning height measurement trick
summary: Measuring height right after waking, when the spine is least compressed, so the number is a little higher than at night.
lead: The morning height measurement trick is the practice of measuring height shortly after waking, when it is at its daily maximum, instead of later in the day. It is discussed on height and looksmaxxing forums as a way to report a higher figure, to track results of height-related interventions consistently, or to decide what a person's 'real' height is .
claims: Morning height is higher than evening height.
Your real height is the average of morning and night.
Glucosamine, core strength and insoles preserve morning height through the day.

name: Grow Taller 4 Idiots
summary: A paid digital guide of stretches, diet and posture tips that promises adult height gain, which medical sources say is not expected after growth plates close.
lead: Grow Taller 4 Idiots is a digital height-increase program sold as a PDF guide through ClickBank. Its sales page names the creator as Darwin Smith, who says he grew from 5 feet 3 inches to 5 feet 10 inches using a method he learned from an older man and later refined over two years .

name: Sprint/HIIT for growth hormone
summary: Sprints and HIIT do raise growth hormone briefly, but no trial shows they add height.
lead: Sprint or high-intensity interval training (HIIT) for growth hormone is a height-related practice in looksmaxxing communities in which teenagers do all-out sprints or interval workouts in the belief that the resulting surge in growth hormone (GH) will help them grow taller. The idea rests on the fact that vigorous exercise is a recognised stimulus of GH secretion.
claims: Sprinting spikes GH, so it makes teens taller

name: Jumping / basketball / swimming for height
summary: Sports like basketball and swimming are said to add height, but no trial tests it.
lead: Jumping, basketball and swimming are sports that some looksmaxxing and height-focused communities say can stimulate the growth plates or decompress the spine and so add height during adolescence. The belief is also popular in general fitness lore, partly because many elite basketball and water polo players are tall.
claims: Basketball, jumping and swimming stimulate the growth plates
Swimming decompresses the spine and adds height

name: Yoga / Surya Namaskar for height
summary: Yoga and Sun Salutations are sold as height boosters; research covers fitness, not height.
lead: Yoga and Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation) are marketed in some height-increase programmes and forum threads as stretching routines that can add height. Surya Namaskar is a flowing sequence of about twelve linked yoga postures associated with Hindu devotion to the sun god Surya.
claims: Surya Namaskar and stretching poses can make you taller

name: Height subliminals
summary: Audio tracks claiming to make you taller; subliminal research shows no height effects.
lead: Height subliminals are audio tracks, often distributed on video platforms, that claim to make listeners taller by playing affirmations or frequencies below conscious attention, typically while sleeping or with music in the background. They are part of a wider genre of appearance subliminals.
claims: Listening to subliminal audio can make you grow

name: Protein-heavy growth diet
summary: Eating enough protein and calories in puberty supports growth; surplus protein is untested for extra height.
lead: A protein-heavy growth diet is an approach discussed in height communities in which adolescents eat adequate or high amounts of protein and calories, often from meat, dairy and eggs, to reach their maximum genetic height. Unlike many height claims, it relates to a documented determinant of growth: childhood nutrition.
claims: Eating enough protein and calories lets you reach your full genetic height
Extra protein beyond normal needs adds height

name: Hidden heel lifts / insoles
summary: Removable inserts that add 1-3 cm instantly; cosmetic use is unstudied, medical heel lifts have trials.
lead: Hidden heel lifts and height insoles are removable inserts placed inside ordinary shoes to raise the wearer by roughly one to three centimetres without the visible platform of high heels. Shoes with thickened insoles or built-up heels made to make the wearer look taller are called elevator shoes.
claims: Hidden insoles add 1-3 cm unnoticed

name: Cuban heel / Chelsea boots
summary: Pointed Chelsea boots with a Cuban heel, a stylish way to gain an inch or two with no study behind the claim.
lead: Cuban-heel Chelsea boots, often called Beatle boots, are ankle-high, close-fitting boots with elastic or zip sides, a pointed toe and a Cuban heel, a moderately raised, tapered, stacked heel. In looksmaxxing and height-focused style discussion they are mentioned as footwear that adds roughly one to two inches through a built-in heel, without the visible bulk of a platform.

name: Platform sneakers
summary: Thick-soled sneakers that add inches fast, with the usual ankle-stability trade-offs.
lead: Platform sneakers are athletic-style shoes with a thick sole that raises the wearer's height. In height-focused style discussion they are described as an easy way to gain extra inches in a casual shoe.

name: Hair volume / quiff for height
summary: Swept-up hair like a quiff, claimed to add height; forum talk is mostly about keeping fine hair fluffy.
lead: Styling hair upward, as in a quiff or pompadour, is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a way to add apparent height and a longer head-to-body line. A quiff has longer hair at the front combed up and back, with shorter sides.
claims: Tying hair up overnight gives 'volume' without product.
Upswept hair makes you look taller.

name: Monochrome and vertical-line outfits
summary: One-colour or vertical-line dressing, said to elongate the look; the supporting illusion research is about lines, not clothes.
lead: Monochrome and vertical-line outfits are a style approach in which clothing in one colour, or with vertical lines, is worn head to toe to create an unbroken line that proponents say makes the wearer look taller.

name: High-rise tailored trousers
summary: Higher waistband plus a tailored hem, said to lengthen the leg line; unstudied.
lead: High-rise tailored trousers sit at or above the natural waist and are hemmed to a clean length. In height and proportion discussions, proponents say they raise the visual waistline and so make the legs look longer relative to the torso.

name: Lean physique looks taller
summary: Lower body fat is said to read as taller; attractiveness research exists but nothing on height perception.
lead: The claim that a lean physique makes a person look taller is common in appearance forums. Proponents say lower body fat creates a longer, narrower silhouette.

name: Lying about height / dating app height
summary: Stating a taller height on a dating profile than you measure; common talk, almost no direct research.
lead: Lying about height, or "height padding", is the practice of stating a taller height than one's measured height on a dating profile or in conversation. In looksmaxxing and dating-advice communities it is discussed as a response to the belief that height strongly affects romantic outcomes, particularly for men (see Heightpill).

name: Heightpill / height blackpill
summary: The belief that height decides a man's dating fate; research shows a taller-partner preference, not an iron rule.
lead: The heightpill (or height blackpill) is a belief, widespread on looksmaxxing and incel-adjacent forums, that a man's height is among the most decisive factors in dating and social outcomes, and that short stature cannot be offset by other traits. The term follows the "pill" vocabulary of online manosphere communities, where a "pill" is a supposedly uncomfortable truth.
claims: Height is the single most decisive trait for a man's dating success.
Looks or other traits cannot compensate for being short.
The importance of height is universal and biological.

name: Mazdutide
summary: Weekly GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist approved in China for weight loss; strong trial data, but regional approval only.
lead: Mazdutide (also IBI362 and LY3305677) is a once-weekly injectable peptide that activates both the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor and the glucagon receptor. It was developed by Innovent Biologics together with Eli Lilly, and received marketing approval in China in June 2025.

name: Orforglipron
summary: Once-daily GLP-1 pill that isn't a peptide; phase 3 weight loss data and a US label, still newer than injectables.
lead: Orforglipron (LY3502970), marketed as Foundayo, is a once-daily oral, non-peptide small-molecule agonist of the GLP-1 receptor developed by Eli Lilly for obesity and type 2 diabetes. Unlike injectable peptide drugs such as semaglutide, it is a small molecule taken by mouth.

name: Oral semaglutide (Rybelsus)
summary: Semaglutide as a daily tablet: proven for type 2 diabetes, with a weight-loss version now approved.
lead: Oral semaglutide, sold as Rybelsus, is a tablet form of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide. It was the first GLP-1 receptor agonist developed for oral administration, co-formulated with an absorption enhancer, sodium N-(8-[2-hydroxybenzoyl] amino) caprylate, that helps the peptide survive the stomach.

name: Garcinia cambogia
summary: HCA-based fat-burner supplement; trials and reviews mostly find weak effects, with some liver-injury reports in blended products.
lead: Garcinia cambogia, now classified as Garcinia gummi-gutta, is a tropical fruit tree native to the Western Ghats of southwestern India. Its fruit rind is used as a sour flavouring in curries, and its principal acid, hydroxycitric acid (HCA), is extracted and sold as a weight-loss dietary supplement.

name: Raspberry ketones
summary: A raspberry-aroma compound sold as a fat burner; human weight-loss evidence is essentially absent and safety data are thin.
lead: Raspberry ketone (4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)butan-2-one, also called rheosmin or frambinone) is a phenolic compound that gives red raspberries much of their characteristic smell. It also occurs in cranberries and blackberries, and is used in perfumery, cosmetics and as a food flavouring.

name: Conjugated linoleic acid (CLA)
summary: A fatty acid from ruminant fat sold as a body-fat reducer; mouse results were striking, but human trials show small or no lasting changes.
lead: Conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) refers to a group of positional and geometric isomers of linoleic acid whose double bonds are conjugated. The most abundant forms are cis-9,trans-11 (rumenic acid) and trans-10,cis-12. They occur naturally in the meat and dairy fat of ruminants, produced by rumen microbes.

name: Forskolin
summary: A Coleus plant compound that raises cAMP in cells and is sold as a fat burner; supplement claims rest on small, low-quality studies.
lead: Forskolin, also called coleonol, is a labdane diterpene obtained from the roots of Coleus forskohlii, a plant in the mint family used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine.  It was identified in the 1970s and became a widely used biochemical tool because it activates adenylyl cyclase and raises intracellular cAMP.

name: Fucoxanthin
summary: A brown-seaweed pigment sold as a fat burner on the strength of rodent data; human evidence is scant and bioavailability appears low.
lead: Fucoxanthin is a xanthophyll carotenoid (C42H58O6) that serves as a light-harvesting accessory pigment in brown macroalgae and diatoms, and gives them their olive-brown colour. It was first isolated in 1914 by Willstatter and Page from brown algae.

name: Glucomannan
summary: Konjac fibre that swells into a gel in the stomach; sold for appetite control, with meta-analyses finding little to no clinically meaningful weight loss.
lead: Glucomannan is a water-soluble polysaccharide and dietary fibre made of beta-1,4-linked mannose and glucose units, found in the cell walls of several plants. The konjac corm is its main commercial source, at about 40 percent by dry weight.
